### Item 133 (2026-09-09)

**M2 lands: the dangling node run is refused at the scanner.**  Item 119's
second mechanism, and the one whose shape is a RUN rather than a token.  A
trailing `[96]* (scalar|alias)?` whose START sits at an OPEN indent level's own
column belongs to nothing: the level is already occupied by the collection that
opened it, so the run is neither that collection's next key nor any indicator's
content, and §9.2 has no production for it.  `scanNextToken_checkDanglingNode`
runs BEFORE the structural dispatch — a dangler dies at a `...`/`---` too
(`a: 1⏎b⏎...`), and the marker would otherwise consume the step — and
`scanLoop_checkDanglingNode` runs beside `scanLoop`'s other two final
validations.

**What separates a dangler from a value is its PREDECESSOR, and that is one new
token predicate.**  `YamlToken.offersNodeSlot` is `:`, `?` and `-` — the three
block indicators whose own productions are followed by `s-l+block-node` or
`s-l+block-indented` — so `a:⏎b` is `{a: b}`, `?⏎b⏎: v` is the explicit key's
content and `-⏎b` is the entry's, at whatever column the content sits.  Behind
anything else there is no slot: a finished scalar (`a: 1⏎b`), a flow close
(`k: [1, 2]⏎b`), or another dangler.  The run's own head is
`YamlToken.isNodeBody` — a scalar or an alias, and NOT the flow closes, which is
where it parts company with `completesFlowValue`: a `]` in block context ends a
collection some earlier line opened, so it heads no run.

**The two arms differ in one conjunct, and the difference is the point.**
Mid-stream the check asks for `simpleKeyAllowed` — a run still on its own line
may yet be resolved by a `:` (`a: 1⏎b: 2`, where `b` becomes a key), and the
flag is down there.  At the end of input there is no `:` left to come, so the
EOF twin does not ask.  That asymmetry is what the first probe got wrong: with
the flag required at EOF, `a: 1⏎b` was missed while `k: 1⏎|⏎  x` fired, because
a block scalar's scan leaves the flag up and a plain walk does not.

**The position reported is the RUN's start, not the cursor's.**  The parser
reports where the offending node begins, and the check reads it off the run's
first token: `a: 1⏎b⏎c: 2` fires at the dispatch of `c` on line 2 and reports
line 1, column 0; `k:⏎  a: 1⏎|⏎  x` fires at the end of input and reports line
2, column 0, the `|`.  A cursor position would have matched neither.

**Measured before the runtime was touched, and that is what made the edit
safe.**  A `firstFire` walk — real preprocess, real structural dispatch, the
candidate predicate evaluated at the dispatch point and again at EOF — over all
**402** suite tests: **7** reach it (236B "Invalid value after mapping", 6S55
"Invalid scalar at the end of sequence", 7MNF "Missing colon", 9CWY "Invalid
scalar at the end of mapping", GDY7 "Comment that looks like a mapping key",
GT5M "Node anchor in sequence", TD5N "Invalid scalar after sequence"), all seven
error tests, all seven producing the byte-identical `.invalidBareDocument` the
parser already produced.  **Zero** false positives.  Over item 119's 21 M2 pins
and a 100-input hand battery: every fire exact, every non-fire either accepted
or refused by a different check.

**The absorption, measured by building it.**  **63** decomposition repairs
across **29** files — **32** where one extra `split` suffices and **31** where
the chain is a `cases`/`generalize` ladder and the check has to be peeled by
hand — plus **84** discharges on the `via_*` and `scanLoop`/`scanFiltered`
chain ladders.  That is more than M1's (41 + 56), and the reason is the
placement: M1's bind sits after the structural dispatch, which most proofs
reach through a single `split`; M2's sits BEFORE it, so it lands in the
preprocess arm of every chain decomposition, `scanLoop` included.  **22** helper
lemmas carry the discharges, in four shapes — the flow context, the
sentinel-only stack, the run-less token array (a flow close ends no run:
`trailingNodeRun?_push_none`), and the converse extractor
`scanNextToken_ok_checkDanglingNode`, which is SIMPLER than item 132's twin
because the check is the step right after preprocessing and needs no
`h_struct`.

**The EOF twin is what the emitter-scannability trees pay for.**  M1's check
never fired at EOF, so those trees only had to carry a premise; M2's does, and
the four `scanLoop`/`scanLoopIx` terminal lemmas now take
`scanLoop_checkDanglingNode s_final = .ok ()`.  Three shapes discharge it:
the sentinel-only stack for a root scalar, and — for the flow documents — the
fact that a `]`/`}` ends no run, which made the outermost-close lemmas grow that

### Item 134 (2026-09-09)

**M3 lands: the `-` at a block mapping's own column is refused at the scanner.**
Item 119's third mechanism, and the last of the refusal half.  A `-` at a column
strictly right of the enclosing collection opens a sequence —
`pushSequenceIndent`'s guard is `col > currentIndent`.  A `-` at a MAPPING's own
column opens nothing, and is legal only where a NODE is expected:
`[183] l+block-sequence(n)` is reached from `[185] s-l+block-indented(n,c)` with
the auto-detected `m` allowed to be 0, so a zero-indented sequence stands
exactly in a node's slot and nowhere else.  `scanBlockEntryValidate` lives
inside `scanBlockEntry`, beside item 48's same-line check and item 31's tab
check, and reports `.invalidBareDocument` at the `-`'s own line and column —
which is where the parser reported, on every one of the 27 probed inputs.

**Two things expect a node, and the check is their disjunction.**  Either the
slot the previous indicator opened is still empty — `nodeSlotAwaited`, which
reads the last real token past a `[96]` run of at most two (`slotHolderIdx?`)
and asks item 133's own `YamlToken.offersNodeSlot` — or a zero-indented sequence
at this very column is already open and this is its next entry
(`sameIndentSequenceOpen`).  Reusing `offersNodeSlot` rather than testing for
`.value` is not tidiness: **the probe refuted the `.value`-only reading on suite
6PBE**, `---⏎?⏎- a⏎- b⏎:⏎- c⏎- d`, where the awaited node is the explicit KEY.
That was the single false positive in the whole 402-input corpus, and it was
found before the runtime was touched.

**M3 is the one mechanism whose test is a BACKWARD WALK, and the walk is bounded
at both ends.**  The entries of a zero-indented sequence are separated from one
another by every token of the collections nested inside them
(`a:⏎- k: 1⏎␣␣m: 2⏎- y`), so "is this sequence still open?" cannot be read off
the array's tail the way M1's and M2's questions can.  Forward, the walk stops
at the first `.blockEntry` at exactly this column — that is the previous entry.
Backward, it stops at the first `.key`/`.value` at a column ≤ this one, and that
bound is not a heuristic: `pushMappingIndent` runs at the column of a `.key`, or
of the `.value` that opens a keyless entry, so the level's own opener is always
reached, and everything behind it belongs to a collection this `-` cannot
continue.  `a:⏎- x⏎b: 1⏎- y` is the shape that needs it — the `.blockEntry` at
column 0 is still in the array, and `b`'s `.key` at column 0 is what says the
sequence it belonged to is over.

**The measurement, run before the runtime was touched.**  The candidate
predicate was evaluated at every dispatch of every input, through the REAL
`scanNextToken_preprocess`, over two corpora.  All **402** suite tests:
**0** hits after the 6PBE correction (**5** before it, all the same test through
its symlinked tag directories).  A generated battery of **3 570** inputs — 42
mapping-opening prefixes × 17 `-` continuations × 5 nestings — **2 023** hits,
of which **1 632** the pipeline already refused with the identical message at
the identical position, **391** it ACCEPTED, and **0** with a divergent
`invalidBareDocument` position.  Every one of the 2 023 was then handed to
PyYAML and to libyaml: **both reject all 2 023**.  That is the check's
soundness, measured against two independent references rather than argued.

**The 391 are a family item 119 never recorded, and closing them CHANGES a
verdict.**  All 391 have one shape — a `-` at the column of a mapping COMPACT IN
A SEQUENCE ENTRY (`- a: 1⏎␣␣- y`, `- ? k⏎␣␣- y`, `- : v⏎␣␣- y`) — and the map
missed them because its `parserGap` predicate only collects what the PARSER
refuses.  Our pipeline accepted them and emitted a spurious empty second
document (`… -SEQ -DOC +DOC =VAL : -DOC -STR`), which is what an accept built on
an artifact token looks like from the outside.  PyYAML and libyaml reject every
one, so this is a correction and not a regression; it is recorded here because
it is a verdict change, and it is invisible to the matrix and to `eventscore`
only because no corpus input has the shape.  `ScannerBlockEntryMappingIndent`
§3 pins the eight representatives.

**The absorption was 21 proofs across 13 files — an order of magnitude under the
map's estimate, and the reason is the LADDER, not the mechanism.**  Item 119
priced a `scanBlockEntry` throw at "276 references"; the references are real,
but every one of them consumes `scanBlockEntry` FORWARD — a hypothesis
`scanBlockEntry s = .ok s'` to be peeled — and not one CONSTRUCTS an `.ok`.  A
new throw on a forward-only ladder costs exactly one `split` per site and no
reasoning: 13 of the 21 are `split at h` + a `contradiction`/`simp` bullet, and
the 8 indexed ones need a `simp only [Bind.bind, Except.bind] at h` first
because their proofs resolve the enclosing `if`s with `rw [if_pos/if_neg]` and
leave the bind unreduced.  M1 cost 41 + 56 and M2 63 + 84 for the opposite
reason: both are binds in `scanNextToken`'s own chain, which the
emitter-scannability trees CONSTRUCT.

**One runtime edit was forced by the desugaring, and it is item 129's rule
pointed at `do`.**  Adding a statement after `scanBlockEntry`'s two
`if … then throw` guards turned the second one into a `__do_jp` join point,
which no `rw [if_pos/if_neg]` and no `split` in the ladders below can see
through — the trace shows `if … then do let __r ← throw …; __do_jp __r else
__do_jp ()`.  The file already states the discipline for `]`/`}` and `&`
("full `else`-chain … so the desugaring is a plain nested `ite` with closed
branches"), and both scanners' `!inFlow` blocks are now else-chains for that
reason, with the reason written where the chain is.

**A gate caught a numbering slip.**  The new annotations first read

printed spec uses; `yaml-spec-1.2.yaml` — the file

`[183]`/`[187]` in the attributes and in the prose around them.  A docstring
citing the other numbering is prose; an `@[yaml_spec]` attribute is a claim the

New guard `ScannerBlockEntryMappingIndent` (52 `#guard` + 10 `example`): §1

`atMappingIndent` with `atSequenceIndent`; §2 item 119's seven pins plus every

### Item 135 (2026-09-09)

**The 16 fallback swaps were 16 in the ledger and are NINE at the compiler, and
they are not one kind of problem.**  Row 19's 1c tightens `[211]`'s
`implicitContinue` from `GOpt SLAnyDocument` to `GOpt SLExplicitDocument`; item
110 built that flip on 2026-09-07 and measured **16 breaking sites, every one in
`StreamAccum`**.  The number has been the ledger's ever since.  Items 111–134
landed in between, so this item re-measured it — twice, with two instruments
that agree.

**Instrument 1: the elaborated environment.**  A walk over every constant in
`StreamAccum` and `DocumentProduction`, collecting each application of
`SLYamlStream.implicitContinue` and classifying its `l-any-document?` argument,
finds **16 applications** — and the classification is what the tightening reads:
one `GOpt.none` (safe at any document type), one `SLAnyDocument.explicit`, one
`.directive`, and thirteen `.bare`.  The walk costs **7 seconds** (the flip below, scripted as
flip → build → revert → rebuild, took **4 min 56 s** end to end), and it sees
what a grep cannot: an application a tactic produced, or one whose document
argument is a bound variable — three of the sixteen were the latter, all of them
`pendingDocStart`'s builder.

**Instrument 2: the flip itself.**  After this item's edits, the constructor was
tightened, `lake build` run, and the file reverted.  Nine errors, all in
`StreamAccum`, at exactly the nine applications the walk had classified as
non-`GOpt.none` — the walk's classification is sound, and the walk is the
instrument the remaining items should use.  The first reads:

```
error: L4YAML/Proofs/Production/StreamAccum.lean:3055:8: Application type mismatch: The argument
  SLAnyDocument.bare sp_mid sp_m
    (SLBareDocument.mk sp_mid sp_m
      (SBlockNode.flowInBlock 0 YamlContext.blockIn sp_mid sp_br sp_ne sp_m h_sep
        (SFlowNode.content 0 YamlContext.flowOut sp_br sp_ne h_content) h_ssl))
has type
  SLAnyDocument sp_mid sp_m
but is expected to have type
  SLExplicitDocument sp_mid sp_m
```

`DocumentProduction.stream_implicit_continue` is a tenth, and the build cannot
reach it: `DocumentProduction` imports `StreamAccum`, so it is never compiled in
a run where `StreamAccum` fails.  Its classification is `.explicit` — the same
wrapper deletion as `structural_dispatch_to_pending`'s.

**Two of the sixteen were dead.**  `flowSeq_extends_stream` and
`flowMap_extends_stream` extended the stream with a completed top-level flow
collection as a bare document — "the grammatical replacement for `scannerDrop`'s
job (Fix A, Piece 2/3)", as their docstring still said.  The flow-open stack has
carried that job since items 44–46.  A second environment walk — which
declarations REFERENCE each of the sixteen sites — returns **zero consumers** for
both, and the same walk shows `nodocMapRoute`/`nodocMapRouteF` (item 116) and
`stream_implicit_continue` unspent as well.  The two extenders are deleted; the
build is the check, and `[1, 2]` and `{a: b}` still parse as documents through
the stack that replaced them.

**Three were one field read at the wrong end.**  `pendingDocStart` handed back a
DOCUMENT — `h_doc_builder : ∀ sp_end, GAlt SLBareDocument (GSeq SENode
SSLComments) sp_scan sp_end → SLAnyDocument sp_block sp_end` — and left
`close_with_ssl`, `accum_flow_open_depth0` and `accum_content_pending` to place
it, each writing out the same `[211]` term around a document whose `[210]`
alternative it cannot see.  The producer can: a standalone `---` builds
`[208] l-explicit-document`, a `%YAML` run builds `[209] l-directive-document`,
and those take DIFFERENT arms of `[211]`.  So the field is a ROUTE now —
`h_doc_route : … → SLYamlStream sp_start sp_end` — the three consumers apply it,
and each producer spends the arm it can justify.  The explicit producer's is the
implicit continuation itself, which is what the tightening keeps.

**Two were the seed's own root sequence.**  `accum_block_on_noPending`'s `-` arm
opened `[183]` under a bare document appended to the accumulated stream.  There
is no accumulated stream to continue: a block-context `noPending` is the
stream's SEED — item 116 counted the constructor's eight producers and the other
seven are flow-interior — so the region behind it is `[202] l-document-prefix*`
and the sequence heads the stream's FIRST document.  `[211]`'s `single` carries
that, and `single`'s `l-any-document?` slot is the one 1c leaves untouched.
Both faces swap: the entry alone and the entry with its `[186]` tail.

**What made that spendable is a premise coming OFF, and the rule is worth
keeping.**  Item 116 wrote the carrier as `h_nodoc : sc.inFlow = false →
sc.documentEverStarted = false → GStar SLDocumentPrefix sp_start sp`, the two
premises naming the two producer families.  They do name them — but the seven
flow sites refute on `inFlow` ALONE (`nodoc_of_flowLevel_succ` never looks at the
second premise) and the seed pays unconditionally, so `documentEverStarted =
false` was load-bearing at NEITHER producer.  At every consumer it is a
scanner-state fact nothing threads.  **A premise no producer spends and no
consumer can discharge is a field that cannot be cashed**: the carrier stood for
nineteen items with zero consumers, and dropping the premise gave it its first
two on the same day.  Item 116's own guard is corrected in place.

**What the remaining nine are, and they are three questions, not nine.**

| sites | what they pass | what they need |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `SLAnyDocument.bare` | the route decision: `single`, `suffixContinue`, a resumed level, or the refusal |
| 1 | `SLAnyDocument.directive` | a head-or-suffix witness on `pendingDirective`, which records none |
| 1 (+1 downstream) | `SLAnyDocument.explicit` | nothing — the wrapper comes off at flip time |

The seven are `topLevelFlowResumeSep`, `rootMapRoute`, `rootMapRouteF`,
`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`, `content_dispatch_after_close` and
`accum_content_pending` twice.  **They wait on one carrier, not seven**: the

REFUTED.  That fourth case is what items 132–134 bought: a completed root node

suffix side for the node and flow faces (`suffixNodeRoute`,
`suffixFlowResumeSep`); the head twins of those two are the only routes still

**The directive residue is a missing witness, not a missing refusal.**
`a: 1⏎%YAML 1.2⏎---⏎b: 2` is refused by both pipelines
(`directive after document content without document-end marker at line 1`), and

### Item 138 (2026-09-10)

**The directive document gets its own `[211]` arm, and the swap surface moves
for the first time in three items.**  Items 136 and 137 gave the landing's route
face its HEAD and MARKER arms and took two whole caller families off the
fallback; neither moved the `implicitContinue` count, because the arms they fed
are shared and an arm goes only when its LAST caller can pay something else.
This item deletes a site outright — the one [item 135](#item-135-2026-09-09)
named and could not fix.

**A directive document has no implicit-continuation reading at all.**  `[211]`'s
implicit continuation carries an `l-any-document?`, so it TYPES a `[209]
l-directive-document` — but `scanDirective` refuses a `%` after content with no
`...`, so no stream ever reaches one that way.  The two readings that exist are
the stream's own head (`single`'s `l-any-document?` slot behind `[202]
l-document-prefix*`) and the slot a `...` opens (`suffixContinue`'s).  Item 135
wrote exactly that and left the site standing, because WHICH of the two holds is
a datum `pendingDirective` did not carry.

**What carries it is the flag `scanDirective` itself reads.**  A `%` reaches
`structural_dispatch_to_pending` only with `allowDirectives` up, and only two
parks can have it up: the stream's own seed (`noPending`, whose `h_nodoc` is the
prefix run item 116 built) and a `...` (`pendingDocEnd`, whose marker over the
accumulated stream is item 117's suffix run).  Every other park is produced PAST
the structural dispatch, where `scanNextToken` has already cleared the flag.  So
the seven other block-context constructors gain `h_nodir : sc.allowDirectives =
false` and REFUTE the premise rather than answering it, `PendingNode.dirRoute`
is that case split, and `pendingDirective` carries the resulting ROUTE — item
135's own reshaping of `h_doc_route`, one production over.

| where | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `structural_dispatch_to_pending`'s `%` | park with no arm | `h_dir_route` resolved from the closed park |
| `structural_dispatch_after_directives`'s `%` | rebuilt nothing | forwards the route along the run |
| `structural_dispatch_after_directives`'s `---` | `implicitContinue` + `SLAnyDocument.directive` | the park's own arm, applied |

**The park's `allowDirectives` face is the item's real cost, and it is paid once
per dispatcher.**  Stating `h_nodir` on the seven constructors raised **50**
sites in **20** lemmas — measured the way items 129 and 130 measure: state the
field, build, read back the distinct sites Lean reports.  None of them argues.
The flag is cleared before the three dispatchers run
(`allowDirectives_update_false`) and none of them writes it again, so
`nodir_of_content_dispatch`, `nodir_of_block_dispatch` and
`nodir_of_flow_dispatch` make every site a ONE-TERM payment — item 47's
`stale_of_dispatch` shape.  Two sites are not a dispatch: `pendingDocStart`'s
two producers answer `rfl` (`scanDocumentStart` clears the flag itself), and
`accum_step_flow`'s two flow closes read the `h_ad_false` their own branch
already had.  `block_dispatch_deferred` has no dispatch equation at all — it is
the escape — so it takes the fact as a premise and its **12** call sites pay it
from theirs.

**What the dispatcher walks cost.**  `ScannerAllowDirectives` had preprocessing
only; the two indicator dispatchers needed their own, and they are the file's
own shape — unfold, split, bottom out in `emit`/`advance`.  Seventeen lemmas:
the two indent pushes and their `ite` forms, `scanBlockEntry`, `scanKey`,
`scanValue` with its two helpers, the four flow scans and `scanFlowEntry`, the
two dispatchers, and `scanDirective_allowDirectives` — the converse the `%`
branch discharges the premise with.

**Measured, both instruments.**  The reference-count walk over the elaborated
terms (imported at `DocumentProduction`, so the closure covers both modules —

how the count reads ten instead of eleven if you are not careful):
`SLYamlStream.implicitContinue` falls from **eleven applications in ten holders**

`structural_dispatch_after_directives`.  Flipping the constructor's `[210]` slot
to `GOpt SLExplicitDocument` gives **eight** errors in `StreamAccum`, down from

```
error: L4YAML/Proofs/Production/StreamAccum.lean:5434:12: Application type mismatch: The argument
  SLAnyDocument.explicit sp sp_end (SLExplicitDocument.withContent sp sp' sp_end h_marker h_content)
has type
  SLAnyDocument sp sp_end
but is expected to have type
  SLExplicitDocument sp sp_end
in the application
  GOpt.some sp sp_end
    (SLAnyDocument.explicit sp sp_end (SLExplicitDocument.withContent sp sp' sp_end h_marker h_content))
```

**The families at the runtime.**  `%YAML 1.2⏎---⏎- a`, `⏎…⏎a: 1`, `…⏎hello`,
the `%TAG` extension and the empty `%YAML 1.2⏎---` are ONE document each on both

**A correction, made where it was written.**  `pendingDocStart`'s docstring (item

### Item 139 (2026-09-10)

**The bare-document fallback gets a name, half its domain is refuted, and the
other half turns out not to be a gap.**  Items 117, 136 and 137 gave the content
landing's route face its SUFFIX, HEAD and MARKER arms; what they left standing
is the fallback — a completed top-level node appended to a FINISHED stream as a
second bare document — and what the fallback owed was items 132–134's refusal,
threaded to the accumulation as a contradiction instead of restated as prose.
This item threads it, and measures that it reaches exactly half.

**Naming it is half the item.**  Three call sites built the same term inline
(`content_dispatch_after_close` and the landing skeleton's two landings), so
`[211]`'s bare reading was three applications with nothing to refute.
`bareNodeRoute` is that term, written once, beside `suffixNodeRoute` and
`nodocNodeRoute` — the fourth sibling, and the one 1c deletes.

**The discriminator is the indent stack, and the two halves fire at different
STEPS.**  That is the item's one real measurement, and it is machine-checked in
the new guard rather than argued: `fireAt` walks the real `scanNextToken` and
reports which §9.2 check fired and at which landing.

| input | fires | at |
|---|---|---|
| `a⏎# c⏎b` | `checkBareDocument` | landing **1** — before `b` is scanned |
| `"x"⏎# c⏎y`, `'x'⏎# c⏎y`, `a⏎# c⏎␣␣b` | `checkBareDocument` | landing 1 |
| `[1, 2]⏎# c⏎b` | `checkBareDocument` | landing 5 |
| `&p a⏎# c⏎b` | `checkBareDocument` | landing 2 (the run's SCALAR completes it) |
| `a: 1⏎b`, `- a⏎b`, `k:⏎␣␣a⏎# c⏎b` | `scanLoop_checkDanglingNode` | **EOF** |
| `a: 1⏎b⏎c: 2`, `a: 1⏎b⏎...` | `checkDanglingNode` | landing 4, one landing LATE |
| `a: 1⏎b: 2`, `- a⏎- b`, `a: 1⏎...⏎b`, `a: 1⏎---⏎b` | — | clean |

At the sentinel alone the landed node is a second bare document and the check
fires AT the landing, so the accumulation step for that node never runs — the
route has nothing to serve, and `bareNodeRoute_or_refused` says so.  With a level
still open the same input is a DANGLING run, and `danglingNodePos?` reads the run
off the TOKEN ARRAY: the run has to be scanned first.  The step therefore RUNS,
the `pendingContent` it makes owes an `h_closable`, and `[211]` has exactly one
reading for it.

**So the surviving half is not a hole in the argument — it is a fact about
1c.**  Row 19's 1c requires `l-document-suffix+` for the bare alternative;
until the dangling window is closed, the accumulation has no witness for
`a: 1⏎b`'s one accepted token and the constructor cannot be tightened.  Closing
it is not a better reading of `[211]`: it is a `danglingNodePos?` face on the
park — the run is already in the token array when the park is made, so the fact
is available where `h_closable` is stated — and that is the item this one names.

**The carrier: `CompletedTail`, and 24 sites in 7 lemmas.**  `StaleNodeTail`
(item 47) is `CompletedTail` plus two LINE facts, `needIndentCheck` and
`simpleKeyAllowed` both DOWN, and neither survives a park AT a line start: the
block scalar ends past a break with the flag up (item 77) and the break sets the
indent check.  §9.2's landing refusal wants the opposite polarity of the flag and
never reads the indent check at all, so the half a park can carry
UNCONDITIONALLY is the half that mentions neither — the token array's own
reading, which is the check's fourth conjunct.  Stating it on `pendingContent`
and `pendingBlockContent` raised **24** sites in **7** lemmas (measured the way
items 129/130/138 measure: state the field, build, read back the distinct sites
Lean reports), and `completedTail_of_dispatch` makes 22 of them a ONE-TERM
payment — item 47's `stale_of_dispatch` shape at the other polarity, with the
block-scalar arm PAYING where that lemma refutes.  The two flow closes read the
`staleNodeTail_scan*End` they already had, through the new projection.

Two parks do NOT get the field, and both `Or.inr`s name a park where the fact is
FALSE rather than one where it is merely unstated: `pendingProps`' tail is a
`[96]` run, and `pendingFlow`'s producer is `block_dispatch_deferred` — the block
INDICATOR dispatch's escape — so the token behind it is a `-`, `?` or `:`.
`completesFlowValue` excludes both by construction, which is item 102's split
read at a third place.

**The three transports, and the stack decides all three.**  Preprocessing has
three writers between the park and the landing: `skipToContent` touches neither
the tokens nor the stack, the unwind is the IDENTITY at size ≤ 1
(`unwindIndents_of_size_le_one` — the loop's own guard wants `1 < indents.size`),
and the save's two reservation placeholders are exactly what `lastRealTokenVal?`
skips.  Above size 1 the transport is FALSE, and that is the same discrimination
again: a landing that pops emits a `blockEnd`, which does not complete a value.

The flag is the third transport and it has two sources.  A park AT a line start
hands its own (`PendingNode.arm_or_col` + `preprocess_simpleKeyAllowed_mono` —
every writer preprocessing has for `simpleKeyAllowed` moves it UP).  A park off
one crossed the break that re-arms it, which is item 76's own hypothesis: so
`preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol`'s landing arm gains a THIRD reading,
`s_prep.simpleKeyAllowed = true`, appended last so item 76's two keep their
projections.  Cost: **5** sites, all `landing_or_park_save`'s callers, and one
signature relax.

**The threading is item 47's, one check earlier.**
`scanNextToken_checkBareDocument`'s success was already in
`scanNextToken_accum_step`'s split chain with no name; one `rename_i` names it,
`accum_step_content` forwards it, and `accum_content_pending` spends it.  The
check runs BEFORE the `allowDirectives` update, so unlike `h_adj` it reads
`s_prep` itself.

**Measured, both instruments.**  `SLYamlStream.implicitContinue` falls from **ten
applications in nine holders** to **eight in eight** — `content_dispatch_after_close`
and `accum_content_pending`'s two collapse into `bareNodeRoute`'s one.  Flipping
the constructor's `[210]` slot to `GOpt SLExplicitDocument` gives **six** errors
in `StreamAccum`, down from eight, at six lemmas: `topLevelFlowResumeSep`,
`rootMapRoute`, `rootMapRouteF`, `bareNodeRoute`,
`structural_dispatch_to_pending` and `accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`.  The named
route's own error is the one that matters:

```
error: L4YAML/Proofs/Production/StreamAccum.lean:4277:32: Application type mismatch: The argument
  SLAnyDocument.bare sp_anchor sp_m (SLBareDocument.mk sp_anchor sp_m h_bn)
has type
  SLAnyDocument sp_anchor sp_m
but is expected to have type
  SLExplicitDocument sp_anchor sp_m
in the application
  GOpt.some sp_anchor sp_m (SLAnyDocument.bare sp_anchor sp_m (SLBareDocument.mk sp_anchor sp_m h_bn))
```

Two of the six are not over-approximations at all: `structural_dispatch_to_pending`'s
is a `---` document continuing a stream implicitly and the flip merely deletes its
`SLAnyDocument.explicit` wrapper, and `DocumentProduction.stream_implicit_continue`
is the same shape (not in the count — the build stops at `StreamAccum`, so that
module is never reached, exactly as at item 138).

**A name collision, caught by the compiler and renamed.**  The predicate was
`NodeTail` for one build.  `LineOpenGuard` already has a `NodeTail` — §7.5's tail
allowlist, a predicate on a CHARACTER — and `StreamAccum` opens that namespace,
so the two resolved only by type.  Renamed to `CompletedTail`, with the reason
in its docstring.

**What remains.**  Three families, and now each has a reason rather than a
label:

* **the dangling window** — `a: 1⏎b`, `- a⏎b`, `k:⏎␣␣a⏎# c⏎b`.  Reached through
  `content_dispatch_after_close` and the landing skeleton's unrefuted arm, and
  the next item is a park face for `danglingNodePos?`, not a route.  **Read this
  with item 140**: scoping that face found that the INDENTED members of this
  family were not refused by the scanner at all — the landing's unwind displaced
  the run before the check saw it — so the face had nothing to contradict until
  item 140 gave the check its two states;
* **the flow lane** — `accum_flow_open_depth0`'s shared `main`, where
  `topLevelFlowResumeSep` is the same fallback for a completed flow collection.
  Its refutation is this item's one dispatcher over: `h_bare` threaded through

* **the block `-` landing** — `accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`'s `rootBlockSeq`,
  and `rootMapRoute`/`rootMapRouteF`, the key routes the same landings take when
  the completed node turns out to be a KEY.  **Read this with item 141**: this
  family is not a peer of the dangling window but its PREREQUISITE.  A park's
  dangling reading is revoked by the same-line `:` — 2272 of 2275 dangling parks
  measured across 490 real YAML files are exactly that landing — and that is the
  one landing where §9.2 gives the accumulation nothing to discharge the reading
  with, so the park face has no home until this landing stops requiring a stream
  through a park the `:` turns into a key.

### Item 140 (2026-09-10)

**§9.2's mid-stream dangling check was reading one writer too late, and the
writer was the landing's own unwind.**  Item 139 measured the bare-document
fallback's surviving half as the dangling family and named a park face for
`danglingNodePos?` as the item that would close it.  Scoping that face found
something first: for the INDENTED half of the family the scanner does not refuse
at all, so there was no refusal to thread — and row 19's 1c could not be closed
at any price while that landing scanned clean.  This item is the refusal.

**The two checks were not the same check.**  `scanLoop_checkDanglingNode` runs
before `scanLoop`'s own `unwindIndents s (-1)`, so it reads the array the run is
still in.  `scanNextToken_checkDanglingNode` ran on the state
`scanNextToken_preprocess` RETURNS — and preprocessing unwinds: it emits a
`blockEnd` for every level the landing dedents past and pops them.  A run whose
own level the landing dedents past is therefore no longer trailing
(`trailingNodeRun?` stops at the `blockEnd`) and no longer sits at any open
column (`indents.any` has lost the entry), so the check read `none`.

**The measurement, at the landing where it happens.**  `readingAt` walks the
real scanner and reports `danglingNodePos?` at BOTH of a landing's states — the
state the landing arrived with, and the state preprocessing returns:

| input | landing | at the run's state | at the landing's state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a: 1⏎b⏎c: 2` | 4 | `some 1,0`, stack 2 | `some 1,0`, stack 2 |
| `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣b⏎c: 2` | 6 | `some 2,2`, stack 3 | **`none`**, stack 2 |

The root landing pops nothing and the two readings are the same one; the
indented landing pops one level and the reading is gone.  That row is the only
place the two disagree in either input — §1 of the new guard pins all six
landings of the second.

**What that cost, before this item.**  `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣b⏎c: 2` scanned CLEAN.
Only `TokenParser.parseStreamLoop`'s `validNextToken` refused it, and at the
same position the scanner would have named — line 2, column 2, the run's own
start.  Both halves of the pipeline therefore rejected the input, so no test
saw anything wrong; what was wrong was WHICH half, and the accumulation is an
invariant about the scanner alone.  Every step the scanner accepts has to come
out of `StreamAccum` with a production, so the indented dangling run's step
owed one, and `bareNodeRoute` — the reading 1c deletes — was the only one
`[211]` has.  A park face cannot refute a step nothing refuses.

**The change is two states on one check.**  The break is a fact about the
LANDING and the run is a fact about the ARRAY, and they are now taken from where
each lives: `scanNextToken_checkDanglingNode s_run s_land`, applied as
`scanNextToken_checkDanglingNode s_run s` at the one call site in `scanNextToken`
and its two indexed twins (`scanNextTokenIx`, `scanNextTokenIxWC`).  `s_run` may
be the state `scanNextToken` was called with, because `skipToContent` writes
neither tokens nor indents: the only writer between the two is the unwind, and
the save's placeholders are exactly what `prevRealIdx?` skips.

**It is a strict narrowing, and the suite says how strict.**  `unwindIndents`
only APPENDS to the array and only POPS the stack, so the post-unwind reading is
`none` wherever the pre-unwind one is — the new check refuses a superset, and
the question is only whether the superset exceeds the parser's.  It does not:
`run-all-tests.sh` **4492/4492**, matrix **402/402** event and **282/282** JSON
on BOTH pipelines, `eventscore` **347/358** with **0** `event-reject` and **0**
`error-miss`, `suiterunner` **869 passed / 0 failed / 151 skipped** — every one
of them unchanged against item 139.  A runtime narrowing that moves no
conformance number is what "the scanner's acceptance is now the parser's" looks
like from the outside.

**Sites: 51, and the autoparam is why it is not 90.**  The check's arity change
reached six categories:

| category | sites |
|---|---|
| the four exemption lemmas + two indexed twins | 6 |
| the two converse extractions (`*_ok_checkDanglingNode`) | 2 |
| the `via_*` dispatch lemmas' `h_dang` hypothesis (4 legacy + 4 indexed) | 8 |
| the `have h_dn : ∃ u, … = .ok u` peels in the step inductions | 14 |
| the exemption lemmas' own call sites (11 legacy + 10 indexed) | 21 |
| `*_eq_of_preprocess`, the pair that says `f` does not capture `s` | 2 |

That last row is the one that could have been expensive.
`scanNextToken_eq_of_preprocess` says "two states with the same preprocessing
result have the same step", and `f` now DOES capture the pre-unwind state — so
the reading has to be a hypothesis, and there are **39 application sites in 8
files**.  Every one of them holds the three field equalities the reading needs,
because the whitespace-walk producers return `tokens`, `indents` and `flowLevel`
in the same bundle as the preprocessing equality — but the DIRECTION differs by
site.  Stating the hypothesis as an autoparam that tries `assumption`, then
`danglingNodePos?_congr` either way round, discharged all **39** with **zero**
call-site edits.  The congruence is the whole content: `danglingNodePos?` reads
exactly three fields and nothing else.

Two seeds pay the sentinel exemption at the stream's first landing
(`init_indents_sentinel` and its indexed twin), where the pre-unwind stack is
the sentinel alone — which is also the half of the domain where item 140 changes
nothing, since `unwindIndentsLoop` wants `1 < indents.size` before it pops.

**One family is NOT this item's, and saying so is part of the measurement.**
`k: [1, 2]⏎␣␣b⏎c: 2` also scans clean and is refused by the parser alone — but
its `b` stands at column 2 with only the root level open, so `danglingNodePos?`
reads `none` at BOTH states and no dangling check can reach it.  That is a
separate over-acceptance at the bare-document boundary, not the one this item
closes, and the guard's §5 names it rather than letting the family look bigger
than it is.

New guard `Tests/Guards/Proofs/ScannerDanglingNodeDedent.lean` (33 `#guard` + 4
`example`): §1 the displacement at both states of the real landing, with the
root landing beside it as the control and the five quiet landings pinned as a
range; §2 the nine-input family, all four readings refusing alike, and the three
positions quoted in full; §3 the check at its two states with each exemption
attached to the state it belongs to, and the EOF twin; §4 seventeen controls
that a dedent must still walk past — the three offering predecessors, the value
one level down, the absorbed plain continuation, the double dedent and the flow
interiors — plus item 133's own two arms unmoved; §5 what it buys and the family
that is not ours.

**What remains.**  The item item 139 named, now with a refusal under it: a
`danglingNodePos?` face on `pendingContent`, spent where `h_closable` is stated.
The shape the face has to take is fixed by the same asymmetry this item
measured — the run is already in the token array when the park is made, so the
park can hold the reading, while the refusal that contradicts it arrives one
landing later (`dangling@6` for §1's input, `eof-dangling@N` at the stream's
end).  That means `h_closable` cannot stay unconditional: the honest shape is the
stream OR the park's own dangling reading, with the consumers refuting the second
disjunct from their own landing's check.  Sizing that is the next item.  **Item
141 sized it**: the shape is right and the cost converges at 32 sites, but four
of the five consumers can refute and the fifth cannot — the same-line `:`, which
is 2272 of 2275 dangling parks in real YAML — so the second disjunct must be
CARRIED through the block landing, and that landing is the prerequisite.  The flow
lane (`topLevelFlowResumeSep`) and the block `-` landing
(`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`'s `rootBlockSeq`, `rootMapRoute`/`rootMapRouteF`)
are unchanged by this item and stand where item 139 left them.

### Item 141 (2026-09-10)

**The park face, sized — and the size is not the finding.**  Items 139 and 140
left one item named: a `danglingNodePos?` face on `pendingContent`, spent where
`h_closable` is stated, so the accumulation can REFUSE `bareNodeRoute` instead of
serving it.  Item 140 gave the mid-stream check its two states, which is what
made a refusal exist for the indented half of the family.  This item scopes the
face and finds that the reading it wants to carry is **revocable**: the park
cannot tell `a: 1⏎b` from `a: 1⏎b: 2`, and the landing that tells them apart is
the one landing where the refusal is not available.

**The two parks are the same park.**  That is one measurement, and it is the
item.

| input | at the park | the next landing | one landing later |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a: 1⏎b` | `some 1,0`, stack 2 | **EOF** | — |
| `a: 1⏎b⏎c: 2` | `some 1,0`, stack 2 | **refused** `invalidBareDocument 1 0` | — |
| `a: 1⏎b: 2` | `some 1,0`, stack 2 | `c=':'` **`ska=false`** | **`none`**, stack 2 |
| `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣b⏎c: 2` | `some 2,2`, stack 3 | **refused** `invalidBareDocument 2 2` | — |
| `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣b: 2` | `some 2,2`, stack 3 | `c=':'` **`ska=false`** | **`none`**, stack 3 |

A completed node parked at an open level's own column reads `some` the instant
its token is appended, and the next `:` takes it back — a run still on its own
line may yet become a key, which is exactly what `simpleKeyAllowed` records and
exactly why the mid-stream check is gated on it.  So the face cannot be a FIELD
the park asserts; it can only be a DISJUNCT the consumer discharges, and §9.2
gives a consumer the means to discharge it in only two places: a landing that
crossed a break (`scanNextToken_checkDanglingNode`, gated) and end of input
(`scanLoop_checkDanglingNode`, not gated at all).

**The census says where the disjunct actually goes.**  Walking the real scanner
over the 490 `.yaml` files in `yaml-test-suite/src` and `examples/`, recording
one observation per state whose `danglingNodePos?` reads `some`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| dangling-park observations | **2275** |
| refused at that landing (`R`) | **2** |
| the stream ended on it (`E`) | **0** |
| survived a landing with the flag DOWN (`D`) | **2273** |
| survived with the flag UP (`U`) | **0** |
| of the 2272 `D`s whose landing is a `:`, at a column other than 0 | **2179** |

~~**99.9 % of dangling parks in real YAML are a same-line `:` with the flag down**~~
— every sibling key of every nested block mapping is one.  [Re-run at
[item 145](#item-145-2026-09-11), which widened §9.2's landing refusal to the
landing's own column, every cell of this table is the same — the corpus rows are
real YAML and all of them rest on a level.]  That is where the
disjunct would have to be CARRIED rather than discharged, and it is the hottest
path in the accumulation, not a corner of it.

**The table above counts the wrong files on the suite side**, corrected
2026-09-13 by [item 156](#item-156-2026-09-13): `yaml-test-suite/src/*.yaml` are
test DESCRIPTORS, each a root sequence of mappings, so the walk counts their own
nested mappings — the same error item 154 made and item 155 corrected at a
different census.  Over the suite's 406 extracted payloads plus `examples/` the
instrument records **346** observations: **8** `R`, **6** `E`, **332** `D`,
**0** `U`.  The carried share is **96 %**, not 99.9 %, and the discharge-able
half is **14** rather than 2 — six of them end-of-input, which a descriptor file
can never produce.  The conclusion is unchanged and never rested on the census:
what decides the face's SHAPE is the revocability table above, which is over
hand-built inputs.  Item 145's re-run repeated the same reading and so repeats
the same correction.

**Two witnesses, both scanning clean, put the carry at a lemma that already
stands flagged.**  `accum_block_pending` builds its `h_close_pending` BEFORE the
case split, so the disjunct reaches it whatever the park is, and its landing may
be the same-line `:`.  `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣b: 2` is the ordinary witness — a nested
mapping's second key.  `a: &x 1⏎*x : 2` is the punting one: `pendingContent`'s
`h_key` packs plain and quoted heads and punts on ALIAS content
(`YamlToken.alias "x"` is the park's last real token, pinned in the guard beside
the packed `ScalarStyle.doubleQuoted` control), so an alias key is where item
102's punt meets a dangling park.  Both reach
`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`, which takes an UNCONDITIONAL stream through a
park the next `:` turns into a key — and that lemma, with
`rootMapRoute` and `rootMapRouteF`, is three of the six errors the `[210]`
constructor flip already reports.

**So this item REORDERS the campaign, the way item 140 reordered item 139.**
Item 139 listed the block `-` landing BESIDE the dangling window as one of three
open families.  It is underneath it: the park face has no home at a same-line `:`
until that landing stops requiring a stream through a revocable park, and the
routes it needs are `bareNodeRoute`'s KEY-side siblings — the reading the same
landings take when the completed node turns out to be a key rather than a node.

**The cost of the face itself, measured the campaign's way** (state it, build,
read back the distinct sites Lean reports), in three waves:

| wave | what was stated | distinct sites |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h_closable` as a disjunct + `PendingNode.close_with_ssl`'s conclusion | **19** (14 producers, 5 consumers) |
| 2 | …+ `accum_block_pending`'s pre-split `have` carrying it | **28** |
| 3 | …+ the four `accum_block_on_*` signatures | **32** |

The waves CONVERGE — 19 → 28 → 32, with `accum_block_pending`'s ten arm sites
going green again at wave 3 — so the face is a finite change and not an
explosion.  ~~What does not converge is the fifth consumer: the other four
(`eof_pending`, `accum_structural_pending`, `accum_content_pending`,

### Item 145 (2026-09-11)

**§9.2's landing refusal was reading the wrong stack fact, and the residue every
landing item recorded was that mistake.**  Items 139 and 142–144 spent

same sentence on its way past: with a level still open the scanner is clean and
only `TokenParser` refuses — item 143's `k:⏎␣␣"a"⏎␣␣[1, 2]`, item 144's

priced a 32-site park face for it.  It was the check's fourth conjunct.

**What makes a landing a second bare document.**  Not that no collection is
open — that the landing stands at **no OPEN LEVEL**.  The completed node already
fills the slot its predecessor offered, so the collection this landing would
roll in has nowhere to go, and the scanner proves it by emitting a second
`blockMappingStart` with no `blockEnd` in front of it:

```
k:                        0,0 blockMappingStart  0,0 key  0,0 scalar "k"  0,1 value
  "x"                     1,2 scalar "x"
  b: 2                    2,2 blockMappingStart   ← the parser's second document
```

The stack holding the sentinel alone is that condition's special case, since
every landing column is `≥ 0` and the sentinel sits at `-1`.  So the conjunct
is now `!(s.indents.any fun e => e.column == (s.col : Int))` in both pipelines
(`scanNextTokenIx_checkBareDocument` is the indexed twin), and the three lane
witnesses are the scanner's refusal at the positions the parser used to report.

### Item 146 (2026-09-12)

**The accumulation carries the indent stack's base, so §9.2's landing refusal
takes ONE stack premise instead of two.**  Item 145 made
`scanNextToken_checkBareDocument` read the landing's own COLUMN, and the
contradiction it supports came out with two stack readings: `h_nopop`, the
landing did not dedent, and `h_open`, the landing stands at no open level.  The
first is a consequence of the second.

**Why the dedent exemption costs nothing.**  A landing that popped rests AT the
column of the entry it popped down to — that is
`preprocess_landing_at_level` (item 127/129), preprocessing's trailing-content
check and the unwind's own terminal condition read together — and that entry is
on the popped stack.  So a landing that popped stands at an OPEN LEVEL by
construction, and `h_open` refutes it outright:

```lean
lemma preprocess_indents_eq_of_no_open_level
    (hok : scanNextToken_preprocess sc = .ok (some (s_prep, c)))
    (h_base : IndentStackBase.SentinelBase sc)
    (h_open : (s_prep.indents.any fun e => e.column == (s_prep.col : Int)) = false) :
    s_prep.indents = sc.indents
```

`h_base` is what makes `preprocess_landing_at_level` unconditional: without it a
stack popped to a single entry rests on something the accumulation cannot name,
and the landing could sit at or right of it; with it that entry is the sentinel
at `-1`, which no landing column reaches.  Item 128 threaded the conjunct
through every scanner STEP and seeded it at `mk'`; what was missing was a
carrier through the grammar ACCUMULATION.

**The carriage.**  `SentinelBase sc` rides `scanLoop_grammar_prod` beside the
other seven facts, seeded by `scan_content_gives_stream_v2` — `mk'_base` plus
the `streamStart` emission and §5.2's BOM, neither of which touches the stack —
and re-established at each step by item 128's `scanNextToken_base`.  It reaches
§9.2's refusal as the sixth conjunct of `BareLandingFacts`.

**Where the premise went was measured before it was written, both ways.**  The
question is whether the four guarded routes take it or the bundle does.  Static
caller closure over `StreamAccum`, comment-stripped:

| the premise is stated on… | declarations | call sites |
|---|---|---|
| the four `_or_refused` routes | **27** | **59** |
| `BareLandingFacts` | **14** | **25** |

### Item 147 (2026-09-12)

**Item 130's next step had a step in front of it, and it was not in the
ledger.**  That item gave the cover its floor and named the two prices of
threading it to the dedent punt — the field (6 sites) and the premise path
(`Mono` and `SentinelBase` reaching the four `:`/`?` producers).  What neither
price covers is whether a producer can PAY at all.  It can only claim
`Covered k [k]` if the landing floored the stack — top at or left of the landing
column — and `preprocess_top_le_col` delivers that with an escape,
`s'.indents = s.indents`.

**The escape is not the pop.**  Reading it as "the landing popped nothing" is
the natural mistake and it is wrong twice over: an unwind that pops nothing
still floors (`unwindIndents_terminal` stops on its own guard), and a landing
that DOES pop is not what a producer knows.  The escape is "the unwind never
ran", which outside a flow is one condition — the indent check was down when
preprocessing reached it.

every `[28] b-break`, `skipToContentLoop_needIndentCheck_mono` keeps it up for
the rest of the walk, and a park that is NOT at a line start reaches a column-0
landing only across a break.  That is the same premise item 76 read at the SAVE
and item 139 at the FLAG.  This item reads it at the FLOOR and appends the floor
to the same landed arm: `skipToContentLoop_anyCol_prod` hands over
`sp.col ≠ 0 → s_result.needIndentCheck = true` (ungated by the flow level — a
break arms the check inside a collection too; only the key's re-arm is §7.4.2's

`s_prep.currentIndent ≤ s_prep.col ∨ s_prep.indents.size ≤ 1`.

**The sentinel rides as a disjunct, and that is what makes the edit free.**
`unwindIndents_terminal`'s other exit is a stack popped to one entry, and ruling
it out is `IndentStackBase.SentinelBase`'s job.  Stating it as a premise on the
splitter was measured first, by adding it and reading back what Lean reported:

**The indicator cannot undo the floor.**  `[187]`'s `?` pushes at its own column

### Item 148 (2026-09-12)

**Item 147 seeded the cover and left it unspendable, and not only for the reason
it named.**  That item said the missing piece was a field on
`ImplicitKeyPack` — true, and this item adds it — but the field alone would not
have been enough, because two of item 147's own readings were wrong for the
consumer that has to spend them.  Both were found by trying to pay, and both are
machine-checked here.

**The bound was the wrong one.**  `pendingMapValue.h_frames` bounded the floor by
the park's own index (`lo ≤ n`).  The landing that SPENDS a cover stands BELOW
that index — that is what a dedent is — and
`preprocess_landing_mem_or_seq` takes `lo ≤ s_prep.col` as a premise — asked
BEFORE the landing's membership is known, since membership is what the lemma
derives.  So the bound has to reach below the landing without naming it, and
`lo ≤ n` does not.  A bound over the WIDTHS does: it drags the floor down to the
outermost width the frames name, and in a chain rooted at column 0 that pins it
AT 0, where the premise is free for any landing whatever (the lemma's own
docstring: "at `lo = 0` the hypothesis is free").  Bounding by the widths alone
fails the other way: where the frames are empty it says nothing, and a floor
free to climb weakens the cover to vacuity (`Covered.raise_floor`).
`IndentStackCover.Floor lo n ks` is both halves —

```
lo ≤ n ∧ ∀ k' ∈ ks, lo ≤ k'
```

— and the guard proves each half is what the other cannot supply: a
counterexample showing the second does not follow from the first
(`lo = n = 2`, `ks = [1]`), and a vacuous witness showing the first does not
follow from the second.  Item 147's DOCS entry is struck and corrected in place.

**And the list was the wrong one.**  The cover a pack carries is over `k :: ks`,
the key's OWN level included, not over `ks`.  The two branches that pay reach it
from opposite sides: a key NESTED below the park opens its level at the `:`
still to come, so its width is free (`Covered.cons`); a key that LANDED on an
open level finds that level already on the scanner's stack and cannot drop it.
Stating the full list is what lets one field serve both, and it is what makes
the `:`'s own push a no-op on the cover — the level it opens is already a frame,
the step names it twice, and `Covered.dedup_head` folds it back.

**The transport is the `:` and nothing else.**  Between a park and the next park
lie a content dispatch (the key) and a `:` dispatch (the value indicator), each
with its own preprocessing.  Preprocessing only pops (`preprocess_cover`) and a
content dispatch writes no level (`dispatchContent_cover`), so the whole of the
carriage is `scanValuePrepare`.  `scanValuePrepare_cover` reports the level it
opens with an EXISTENTIAL, which is all a step-generic caller can say; a caller
holding the live key holds its column, and that is the difference between
`c :: ks` for an unknown `c` and the `k :: ks` the frames already name.  The
named form takes the key-or-`?`-line arm as its premise — which is exactly what
rules out `[196]`'s keyless push at the cursor — and
`scanValueClearKey_arm` supplies it whichever way the clear goes.

**What pays.**  The two root `:`/`?` producers seed, as in item 147, now on both
frame faces — `h_closeF` needs the cover as much as `h_frames`, because the key
dispatch's NESTED branch reads the one and its DEDENT branch the other, and two
existentials cannot be identified after the fact.  The NESTED branch of both key
dispatch lemmas pays the pack: the landed key's width joins the caller's frames
for free and the floor stays strictly left of it (`n < w` on that branch).  Both
implicit `:` producers spend the pack into the next park's two faces.  **So the
chain closes**: every hop is discharged, and none of the payments is conditional
on anything the accumulation cannot supply, so a cover seeded at a root is
carried through every nested implicit key on the way down — which is what the
field was for.

**What does not pay, and why it is not an unthreaded premise.**  The DEDENT
branch does not.  The level the landing popped TO is still on the scanner's
stack, so the pack's cover there is over `w :: ks'` while the caller's is over
the whole of `ks` — and `ResumeFrames.resumeAt` drops every width above `w`.
Reading the one as the other wants three things at once: the stack's SHAPE
(`Mono`, which item 147 threaded through the BLOCK lane and which the CONTENT
lane does not carry), the landing's own floor, and `resumeAt`'s widths as a
sublist of the ones they came from — **item 149 corrects the last of these**: a
sublist is the half the FLOOR spends, and the half the COVER spends is the
opposite direction, COMPLETENESS, that nothing below the landing was dropped.
None of the three is at that branch.  A
fresh document's root, a SEQUENCE park and the flow OPEN pay `Or.inr trivial`
for a different reason: they have no carried stack to inherit, and the chain is
seeded at the `:`/`?` producers, which is where `Mono` rides.

**The price, measured.**  The field is stated at **14** places — the two packs,
the park's two frame faces, the two implicit producers' premises, the two key
dispatch lemmas' `h_nodeF`, their two local build helpers, and the two relays'
pair, twice — and the edit touched **19** declarations in `StreamAccum`.  The
transport is **5** `h_cov_step` helpers, one per lemma that crosses a dispatch,
and **8** new declarations in `IndentStackCover`: the `:`'s three
(`scanValueClearKey_arm`, `scanValuePrepare_cover_key`, `scanValue_cover_key`),
`Covered.dedup_head`, and `Floor` with its three.  One existing guard
(`ScannerPropsLandingSiblingResumes`) projects past the new conjunct.

**What did NOT move, and could not.**  `SLYamlStream.implicitContinue` is FIVE
`[210]` flip errors at the same five holders (`topLevelFlowResumeSep` 3232,
`rootMapRoute` 4501, `rootMapRouteF` 4524, `bareNodeRoute` 4693,
`structural_dispatch_to_pending` 6026 — the same declarations item 147 measured,
at their new line numbers); the raw-route census is TWO
(`content_dispatch_after_close`, `flowKeyRoute_of_root`).  No runtime file
changed, which `run-all-tests.sh` makes checkable rather than asserted: ~~`docs/`
regenerates BYTE-IDENTICALLY~~ — **corrected by item 149**, which measured it:
**62 of the 63** generated files are byte-identical and `coverage-summary.json`
differs only in its `date`.  (A clean `git status` cannot establish either
sentence: `docs/` is in `.gitignore`.)  No scanner verdict moved.

### Item 149 (2026-09-12)

**The dedent landing spends the cover.**  Item 148 carried a cover from a root
down an unbounded chain of nested implicit keys and left ONE branch punting:
`entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s dedent, where the landing pops to a level below the
park's own.  That branch now pays, and so does its props twin.

**The obstacle was real and the reading of it was one half short.**  Item 148
named three things the branch would need — the stack's SHAPE in the content
lane, the landing's own floor, and `resumeAt`'s widths *as a sublist of the ones
it popped from*.  The first two stand.  The third names one of the two halves,
and not the one that was missing.  A sublist is exactly what the FLOOR spends —
`Floor.pop_to`: every surviving width was a frame the park had already bounded,
so the bound travels without being re-measured.  What the COVER spends is the
other direction, completeness: given a level the scanner still holds strictly
below the landing, is it still one of the frames?  A sublist cannot answer that
(`[]` is a sublist of every list), so on item 148's reading the branch would
have paid the floor and stalled at the cover.
`ResumeWidths ks ks' j := ∀ k', k' ∈ ks' ↔ (k' ∈ ks ∧ k' < j)` states what the
popped list IS, and both halves fall out of `ResumeFrames.resumeAt`'s own
recursion with no new premise: the strict decrease each `level` constructor
carries is visited at exactly the steps the pop descends through.  Item 148's
text is struck and corrected where it stands, and the three readings are
machine-checked side by side in the new guard's §1 — `[]` satisfies the bound
`∀ k' ∈ ks', k' < 2`, `[]` is a sublist of `[4, 2, 0]`, and
`¬ ResumeWidths [4, 2, 0] [] 2`.

**What reads one list as the other is the landing's floor, not a list fact.**
The park's cover is over the whole of `ks`; the pack the landing opens carries
`w :: ks'`, and `ks'` holds none of the levels above `w`.  Those levels are not
dropped from the cover by fiat — preprocessing's unwind POPPED them, so the
stack the dispatch receives has nothing above `w` left to name.  That is a
statement about the TOP, and `Mono` is what turns it into one about every entry:
`IndentStackCover.Covered.pop_to`.  The frames' own bound does not move at all
(`Floor.pop_to`): `w` is one of the widths the park already bounded, and so is
every width the landing keeps.

**Which half of `Floor` pays here is worth recording.**  `Floor.pop_to` reads
the WIDTHS half (`∀ k' ∈ ks, lo ≤ k'`) twice and the index half (`lo ≤ n`) not
at all — so the conjunct item 148 ADDED is the whole of what the dedent spends,
and the conjunct it inherited from item 147 is spent at the NESTED branch
instead (`Floor.mono_index`).  The two branches of the key dispatch are what
make both halves live, which is the same reason `h_closeF` and `h_frames` both
have to carry a cover.

**`Mono` is load-bearing, and the guard says so by refuting the lemma without
it.**  A three-entry stack `[-1, 5, 1]` has its top at 1; every remaining
hypothesis of `Covered.pop_to` holds of it at `w = 1` — the top bound, the
cover `Covered 0 [5, 1]`, and the keep condition, which is vacuous because no
frame of `[5, 1]` is strictly below 1 — and the conclusion `Covered 0 [1]` is
false, since the entry at column 5 is not named.  So the payment is not carrying `Mono` for
symmetry with item 147.

**The floor came free.**  `landing_floor_of_arm` (item 147) turns the landed
arm's fourth conjunct into `s_prep.currentIndent ≤ s_prep.col`, and the pack
lemmas already destructure `preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol` to get that arm.
So the content lane's new premise is only the pair item 147 gave the indicator
lane — `(Mono sc ∧ SentinelBase sc) ∨ True`, the same shape as

### Item 150 (2026-09-12)

**The value-line stack carries its cover.**  Items 147–149 gave the STREAM lane
a cover and taught the dedent landing to spend it.  The value-line lane — the
frames an open `[186]` explicit key leaves standing, bottomed at the `?`'s own
unpaid value line rather than at the finished stream — carried none, on either
face, and item 149 listed it as the next thing that could pay.  It does now, at
both pack lemmas, with item 149's `dedent_cover_of_landing` called verbatim.

**One thing does not mirror, and it is the floor's index.**  The stream faces
bottom at the stream and carry `Floor lo n ks`.  These bottom at the `?`, whose
own level is deliberately NOT one of their frames — resuming there is the
entry's unpaid value line, not a sibling — so a cover over them cannot stand at
the park's own floor.  At the seed it is `ks = []` and the `?` has just pushed a
mapping level at `k`: `Covered k []` would have to fail to name it, and does.
One column above it is true, and it is not a vacuity — it says the push left
nothing at or right of `k + 1`.  So these faces carry `Floor lo (n + 1) ks`,
`IndentStackCover.covered_nil_of_top_le` is the seed, and a floor stated at `n`
would have been payable by nobody.  All four readings are machine-checked side
by side in the new guard's §1, the seed's `Mono` premise refuted on item 149's
own `[-1, 5, 1]` stack.

**The rest of the lane is item 148's shape and item 149's lemma.**  The chain's
hop climbs the index by one (`Floor.mono_index (Nat.le_succ k)`) and leaves the
floor where the producer put it; the nested branch conses the landed width, `n <
w` carrying `lo ≤ n + 1 ≤ w`; the dedent branch calls
`dedent_cover_of_landing`, which reads `Floor`'s WIDTHS half and never its
index — which is exactly why the lane's higher index rides through it with no
new lemma at all.  The two lanes' lists stay independent: the membership test
and the payment are both taken twice, because a landing width can name a level
in one stack and not the other.

**The seed came off a measurement already being taken.**
`indicator_cover_at_col` proved the top's bound and then read it ONE way;  it
now names the top and reads it twice, so the `?` producer's value-line payment
costs the walk nothing.  `question_open_map` gains the second reading as a
premise (`h_cov_nil`), and `colon_open_map` — a `[189]` empty-key entry, with no
explicit frame over it — keeps the `Or.inr trivial` it already paid.

**The price, measured.**  **ONE** new declaration, `covered_nil_of_top_le`, and
the stats bear that out exactly: proofs, library and env each move by **+1**.
One conclusion is widened (`indicator_cover_at_col`, now a pair), one premise
added (`question_open_map.h_cov_nil`), and **16** field shapes gain the cover
conjunct — **10** at `n + 1` (the park's two faces, the four pack-lemma premises
and the four relay faces) and **6** at the pack's own index (`ImplicitKeyPack`,
`PropsKeyPack`, both `colon_open_map` route faces and `content_dispatch_routed`'s
two).  Nine destructurings widen to match, three covers step across
preprocessing's pops beside the stream twin already doing it, and three places
punt where there is no slot to punt into: the flow twin at
`flowKeyPack_of_close`, the props close that drops back to it, and
`resumectx_of_landing` — which has no cover slot on EITHER lane, so the value
face is projected there exactly as item 149 left the stream face.  **613**
insertions, **64** deletions, one new guard file.

**Item 149's own forecast was wrong about what comes next, and the correction is
one line of Lean.**  It named the membership split — `by_cases hmem : w ∈ ks`,
which `preprocess_landing_mem_or_seq` would derive — as the only punt left about
the landing rather than the caller.  `KeyPackPunt.dedent` takes no argument, so
the punt disjunct is inhabited at every state; the branch therefore already

membership from the cover cannot add one input to that set.  It can only

KeyPackPunt s := KeyPackPunt.dedent`, and a counterexample to
`Floor lo n ks → w < n → lo ≤ w`), and item 149's DOCS and guard are struck and
corrected where they stand.

**And item 149's axiom sentence was incomplete.**  It said the only non-standard
axioms anywhere downstream are the `native_decide` ones from `ScalarProduction`'s
plain-scalar lemmas and `StructureProduction`'s anchor-name loop.
`dispatchBlockKey_full_prod` and `dispatchBlockValue_full_prod` — in

### Item 151 (2026-09-12)

**The resuming key context carries the landing's cover.**  Items 149 and 150
closed naming the same gap, in the same words: `ResumeKeyCtx` — the context a
landed SIBLING key is handed when the park that closed under it kept its frames
— had no slot for a cover on either lane.  So the one relay that holds BOTH of
the stack's readings, `accum_content_on_pendingMapValue_indented`'s dedent,
projected both of them away on the way in.  This item gives the context a slot
on each lane, pays them at that relay, and spends them into the two pack fields
`content_dispatch_routed` builds.

**The context's floor index is the PACK's, on both lanes — which is where the
value lane stops mirroring its parks.**  A park's value-line frames exclude the
`?`'s own level, so their cover stands one column above the park (item 150).
The key THIS landing heads is a mapping level of either stack, so nothing is
excluded here: `Floor lo k (k :: ks)` is what both faces carry, the same shape
the pack field takes.  The guard's §1 checks the discrimination on a three-entry
stack — a `?` at 0 with a key at 2 — where `Covered 1 []` is FALSE (the key's
level is open and unnamed) and `Covered 1 [2]` is true.

**The index on the way IN is forgotten, and that is what makes one payer serve
both lanes.**  The incoming faces are bounded at different indices by
construction — `n` on the stream lane, `n + 1` on the value lane — and the hop
reads neither of them: `IndentStackCover.Floor.pop_to` spends the WIDTHS half
alone.  So both faces hand the payer `∃ lo n, Floor lo n ks ∧ Covered lo ks sc`,
with the index existential, and item 150's deliberate stagger costs this item no
second argument.

**The one new declaration is a factoring, not an addition.**
`dedent_cover_of_floor` is the arithmetic item 149's `dedent_cover_of_landing`
performs, with that lemma's two escapes taken OUT of it — a caller that cannot
measure its stack, and a park at a line start whose walk armed no unwind.  Both
are about REACHING the floor, not about the hop, so a caller that has discharged
them wants the payment and not a disjunction to case on.  `dedent_cover_of_landing`
now calls it, so the hop is authored once; and the new lemma's conclusion is a
plain `∃`, which is the interrogability this item actually buys — a consumer can
tell that it was paid, where `∨ True` can never be interrogated after the fact.

**Where the payment stands, and why it is reachable there.**  The relay's park
is off a line start by its own field (`h_col0_old : 0 < sp_scan.col`), so the
walk that carried it to column 0 crossed a break, the break armed the indent
check, and preprocessing's unwind ran — which is the landing arm
`preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol` returns in its landed disjunct, and the
input `landing_floor_of_arm` wants.  The other disjunct is the step that stayed
on the line, which this landing is not; refuting it costs more than the punt it
would replace, so it punts.

**§4 measures the lane, and the measure discriminates.**  Item 99's own dedent
(`k:⏎  :⏎b: 2`), four deeper twins, and two whose park is a BLOCK SCALAR — which
ends past a break, so the park sits AT a line start — give **68** states and
**7** pops, all **7** with the landing's own floor and **5** of the 7 off a line
start.  The two that are not are where the derivation punts, and the split is
the point: the scanner establishes the floor at all seven, so item 147's escape
is about what the PROOF can reach and not about what the landing does.

**The price.**  ONE new declaration, `dedent_cover_of_floor`, which item 149's
lemma now calls; the stats move by **+1** on proofs, library and env, which is
what a factoring plus nothing else looks like.  `ResumeKeyCtx` gains two
conjuncts, `resumectx_of_landing` a correspondence argument, cover conjuncts on
its two faces and a payer; `content_dispatch_routed` gains one lift and two
spends.  **705** insertions, **55** deletions, one new guard file.  Of the seven relays that build a resuming context, ONE pays and six
hand the punt — and each of the six names a different missing thing rather than
a different input.

**What still does not pay**, all three of them CONSTRUCTOR fields, which is why
none is a line in this item:

* **The sequence park.**  `accum_content_on_pendingBlock_indented` relays
  `pendingBlock.h_closeF`, which carries the widths alone, and the relay holds
  neither `Mono` nor `SentinelBase` to pay a cover with.  Both the field and
  that thread are what a payment costs there.
* **The skeleton's two parks.**  `pendingContent.h_framesS` / `.h_framesV` and
  `pendingBlockContent.h_closeF` are the faces `h_defer_split` passes, and none
  of the three has a cover conjunct.
* **The park at a line start**, item 147's residue, measured above.

### Item 152 (2026-09-12)

the item is small.**  What a landing's payment needs is `s_prep`'s own floor,

### Item 155 (2026-09-13)

**The sequence lane gets frames, and then a cover.**  Items 152 and 153 left one
entry on the menu: `pendingProps.h_closeFE`, `pendingBlockContent.h_closeF` and
`pendingBlock.h_closeF`, "one chain carrying widths alone", with the sequence
park's relay owing a `Mono` and a `SentinelBase` besides.  This is that entry —
and measuring it first showed the entry was **mis-stated**.

**A cover over an empty list is spendable nowhere.**  The landing's hop is
`ResumeFrames.resumeAt`, whose premise is `j ∈ ks`: a landing resumes only at a
width the frames NAME.  Flipping `pendingBlock.h_closeF`'s escape from `True` to
`False` reports **six punts of seven producers**, and the seventh —
`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`'s landed `-` — pays `ks = []`.  So the lane's
frames were empty wherever they existed at all, and the three fields' missing
cover was never the residue.  The FRAMES were.

**Where a non-empty list exists is the mapping value the sequence fills.**  A
landed `-` on a `pendingMapValue` opens the collection that becomes the awaited
node, and the mapping level the park stands in is still open underneath it —
which is what that park's `h_closeF` has said since item 108, cover included.
`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock` closes the park before its `-` arm runs, so the
item carries that reading past the close as `h_valF`, and the sequence park's
frames become `nv :: ks`.  `k:⏎␣␣- a⏎b: 2` now resumes the mapping the sequence
was written inside instead of re-opening at the root.

**The side condition is `[183]`'s `m` read as a bound**, and its failing case
cannot arise.  `nestedBlockSeq` wants `nv ≤ k` and the frames are strictly
decreasing, so the payment runs at `nv < k` and keeps item 99's bottomed reading
otherwise.  The shape that fails it is `seq-spaces` — a sequence at its key's own
column (`k:⏎- a`) — and there the `-` pushes NO level: the stack stays `[0M]` and
the state never has the shape the payment asks about.  **The one shape that
cannot pay is the one shape that cannot reach the premise**, which is item 154's
finding at a different field.

**Census, by the compiler.**  `h_valF` flipped to `∨ False` distinguishes its
callers by the argument each error names: **9 punts** (`trivial`) and **2
payers** (`h_closeF155`), the two branches of `accum_block_pending`'s
`pendingMapValue` arm — the only park that awaits a node when a block indicator
lands on it.  Flipping the cover conjunct on both the field and the local that
pays it gives **exactly two errors, and they are the two `ks = []` fallbacks**:

**The floor is bounded at the field's own index, and that buys one more hop.**

checks it is `danglingPark_refutes_landing` and `danglingPark_refutes_eof`.

array's last real token is a `blockEnd` rather than the park's own tail — and a
`blockEnd` offers no slot either.  Stating the premise at the reading the lemma
actually spends leaves that transport available; stating it as `CompletedTail`
would have closed the popping half out by construction.

### Item 158 (2026-09-13)

**The property lane's reading, derived — and the half of it that scans clean.**
Item 157 named `pendingProps` as the gate's residue and recorded the lane as one
item, on the strength of four witnesses the scanner refuses.  This item lands the
producer half, takes the character premises off everything item 156 built, and
measures that claim — which is **half true**.  The half that is not is why the
field item 157 named cannot simply be added, and it was found by running the
lane rather than by reading it.

**The dispatcher's token census, in ONE statement.**
`dispatchContent_tokens_push_prop` says a `&` pushes one `.anchor` and a `!` one
`.tag`, at the dispatch's own `currentPos`; `dispatchContent_tokens_push_node`
puts it beside item 156's body arm, and there is no third arm.
`trailingNodeRun?_push_prop` is `trailingNodeRun?`'s property arm — a property
pushed on top starts a trailing run of ONE with the array's own last real slot as
its predecessor, exactly as a body does.  So `danglingPark_of_dispatch` and its
three spent forms lose their `c ≠ '&'` and `c ≠ '!'` premises, and
`ContentRouteGate`'s LEFT disjunct loses them with it:

```
before:  (c ≠ '&' ∧ c ≠ '!' ∧ danglingNodePos? s' = none) ∨ (c = '&' ∨ c = '!')
after:                        danglingNodePos? s' = none  ∨ (c = '&' ∨ c = '!')
```

What the right disjunct names is therefore no longer "the two property
characters" but the STATE they park in.  The refutation is character-uniform
now — given the reading, a `&` landing on an open level behind a completed node
is refuted exactly as a scalar one is — and what is missing at `&`/`!` is a
FIELD.

**The lane splits, and item 157's four witnesses are one half of it.**  All four
are BLOCK-bodied, and all four are refused at the RUN's start, which is the
property:

| shape | scanner | parser |
|---|---|---|
| `a: 1⏎&p b`, `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣&p b`, `- a⏎&p b`, `a: 1⏎!!str b` | refused at the run's start | same position |
| `a: 1⏎&p [b]`, `a: 1⏎&p {b: 1}`, `a: 1⏎!t [b]`, `- a⏎&p [b]` | **SCAN-OK** | refused at `1,0` |
| `a: 1⏎[b]` (no run) | refused — §8.1's floor | same position |

Two mechanisms miss the flow-bodied half and they miss it for different reasons.
§9.2's end-of-input check reads `trailingNodeRun?`, and a `]` is neither a body
nor a property — so once the collection closes the array ends in no node run at
all: at `a: 1⏎&p [b]` the props park reads `some 1,0` and the very next step, the
`[`, reads `none`.  And §8.1's floor, which refuses the same shape WITHOUT a run,
measures the BRACKET's column — which the property run has moved right.

**So the props park really does owe an unconditional route**, and the face item
157 named cannot be a premise on `pendingProps.h_route` as it stands.  The route
has three consumers: `PendingNode.close_with_ssl` would pay from item 157's own
`h_nd` for free; `accum_content_pending` would pay from the next park's premise
one push later; `accum_flow_open_depth0` is the flow ride above and can pay
nothing, because the input it serves is live.

**The second consumer has its own obstacle, and it is about the token array.**  A
property run's reading transports across a BODY push — the walk-back reaches the
same run start — but not across a PROPERTY push, because the start MOVES.
`trailingNodeRun?` walks back over properties with no line filter, while
`trailingPropertyRunOnLine` (which the `[96]` guards read) has one, so a run may
span a break: at `&a⏎!t &b x` — **SCAN-OK**, parser-refused at `1,3` — the token
run starts at the `&a` on line 0 until the third property pushes the start down
to the `!t` on line 1.  The same three properties on one line are refused
(`invalidNodeProperties '&' 0 6`), so the shape exists only because of the break.
A premise stated as `danglingNodePos? sc = none` therefore does not relay through
the run's own extension, which is what the next item has to solve.
